name: FluxIO
baseline: Boost.Asio C++20 file I/O and Go os.O_DIRECT with goroutines (not POSIX pread/pwrite)
workload: 4KiB O_DIRECT sequential/random read and write at queue depths 1-128 on a physical consumer NVMe SSD, io_uring with SQPOLL and fixed buffers.
claimed_speedup: Peak: sequential write 715,827.6 IOPS vs Go 239,383.5 and Boost.Asio 86,783.1 (2.99x and 8.25x); random read 434,377.9 vs Go 308,629.1 and Asio 22,192.8; sequential read 0.92x vs Go. Random write at QD128 429,229.3 IOPS vs 29,074.7 (Go) and 28,411.3 (Asio) unmanaged sparse files

caveats: Baselines are Boost.Asio file I/O and Go, not POSIX pread/pwrite or plain io_uring; the README says IOPS per core is roughly equal to Go; sequential read is slower than Go. First-party, no CPU model. Asio and Go were unmanaged sparse files in the ext4 inode-lock comparison.
